card.title: 175th INFANTRY REGIMENT
card.text: Deployment: Choose a card in hand. Put it on top of your deck.
card.flavorText: The 175th Infantry Regiment is a unit of the US Army, active since 1774, which makes it the seventh oldest regiment in the United States. It had already served in numerous conflicts before WWII, including the Revolutionary War and WWI. The regiment was mobilized in January 1941 and trained in the US before sailing to England in October 1942 aboard the RMS Queen Elizabeth. It spent months preparing for the invasion of Europe, training in Cornwall and conducting amphibious drills at Slapton Sands. The 175th regiment landed on Omaha Beach on 7 June 1944, a day after D-Day, as part of the 29th Infantry Division, tasked with capturing the village of Isigny. It fought its way through thick hedgerows toward Saint-Lô, meeting strong German resistance. At Hill 108, later known as "Purple Heart Hill," the 1st Battalion held its position while nearly surrounded. After securing Saint-Lô, the regiment joined the assault on Brest, targeting German submarine bases. In early 1945, it helped capture Jülich in western Germany, and later took part in the occupation of Mönchengladbach. On 2 May, a patrol from the 175th met Soviet troops near the Elbe River. The regiment remained in Germany with the 29th Division until January 1946, before returning home and reactivating later that year.
